Hi Alice / Acme security team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to learn more about Acme's production use of models for customer support routing. As promised, a quick recap and proposed next steps on the privacy/compliance items we discussed: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (security) in Q1 2026. I attached a short summary (Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf). We're happy to provide a redacted report under an NDA if needed.

2) DPA & SCCs: Per our discussion, we'll provide a standard DPA and propose the SCC module that aligns with the controller/processor relationship. From what you described (Acme is the controller; Redwood will process customer data on your behalf), the typical path is controller->processor SCCs.

3) Vendor questionnaire: I attached the completed vendor security questionnaire (Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) — I filled the tech/security sections we talked through and left legal items blank for your team.

Next steps I propose: 
- Marissa to share Redwood DPA draft and confirm SCC module recommendation (this thread).
- Acme legal to review DPA / indicate preferred redlines.
- Initiate any redacted SOC 2 exchange if legal needs the full report (we can send via secure link/NDAs).
- Schedule 30-min follow-up with legal/security if you'd like to go over DPA redlines.

Can you share the best legal contact + timeline you prefer for DPA review? We can target signing within 2–3 weeks if that works.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the fast turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

- We received the completed questionnaire — thanks. Legal will want to review the DPA and proposed SCCs. Can you confirm which SCC module Redwood intends to use? Our standard playbook requires the controller->processor SCC (module for controller to processor) and affirmative statements in the DPA about subprocessors, data retention, and audit rights.

- SOC 2: Redacted report is fine; we can execute an NDA for the full copy.

- One more item: is Redwood able to support EU data residency / tenant isolation if we need it for some EU customers?

For legal contact, please send the DPA to: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@acme.com> (cc'd on legal@acme in the next email). We typically aim to complete DPA review in 7–14 business days depending on redlines.

Thanks,
Acme Security Team

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Quick internal note based on Acme's questions: 

- Controller/Processor role: For the configuration Marissa described (Acme controls prompts, accounts, and customer data flows; Redwood provides inference and stores minimal telemetry), Redwood is the processor and Acme is the controller. We should therefore propose the controller-to-processor SCCs. In our internal naming that's the "Controller->Processor" module (commonly referenced as Module 2 in the SCC set).

- DPA: Use our standard DPA baseline (I attached the current template to the internal thread). Make sure we include: subprocessors list & process for notification, audit rights clause (redacted SOC2 link allowed), data retention/return or deletion obligations, and transfer mechanisms (SCCs + any supplementary measures).

- EU data residency: We have VPC/private deployment options but need to flag that enabling EU-only residency for a subset of data will require our Private deployment path (and a separate SOW). For sales, mention we can discuss a timeline and cost estimate; for initial signing we can leave data residency as an optional appendix.

Next steps for Marissa: send DPA draft and explicitly call out controller->processor SCCs; propose sending SOC 2 redacted report under NDA. I can join the legal call if needed.

Thanks — Rishi
VP, Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
